text:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: elevated errors + tail latency for /v1/generate (hosted-prod-us-west-2). error_rate +7.8% vs baseline, p95 6.2s (was 1.9s), 30% increase in queue depth. Paging on-call.

Sara.k: paging in — looking at tracing and infra dashboards now. Any recent deploys to runtime? :eyes:

ajay: I pushed a small runtime metrics change earlier but it was just observability tags, not path-critical. Will check backend pools.

miguel: I see sustained KV cache miss storm for llama-35b-q4v2 on node pool gpu-pool-3. KV miss ratio jumped ~x4 around 12:05 UTC — likely more compute per request, causing longer per-token times and queue buildup.

Sara.k: okay, plan: 1) quick mitigation to reduce incoming load 2) isolate noisy model -> route to slower capacity 3) tune runtime max-inflight and timeouts. Starting step 1.

ajay: propose: apply rate limit at edge: set per-tenant burst=30, sustained qps=8 for non-enterprise tier, and reduce shared streaming window to avoid large pinned connections. Anyone object?

Diane: +1. That should blunt the spike quickly. Also recommend disabling embeddings endpoint for heavy requesters temporarily (we can roll it per-customer).

Sara.k: ok executing edge config now. Command:
```
POST /admin/edge/rate_limits/update
{ "scope": "hosted-prod-us-west-2", "rules": [{"selector":"tier:free,api:*", "qps":8, "burst":30}]}
```

deploy-bot: edge config update started (change_id: cfg-2026-17585).

miguel: while that's rolling, I'll start diverting llama-35b-q4v2 traffic for known high-cpu customers to a low-priority fallback model (llama-35b-q4v2-quant, lower mem but slower). Routing rule: if request size > 8k tokens OR tenant in noisy_list -> route to fallback.

ajay: also bump runtime max_inflight per-worker from 64 -> 32 for the affected pools to reduce head-of-line blocking and force quicker shedding on overload. Will apply to gpu-pool-3 only. Command:
```
rltool set --pool gpu-pool-3 --param max_inflight=32 --param request_timeout_ms=45000
```

Sara.k: good. Note that lowering max_inflight may increase rejection rate briefly but prevents large queues. We should pair with graceful reject message so SDKs surface 429 with retry-after.

cs-lead: which customers are impacted? I'm seeing increased errors for acct-omega and acct-zenith (both heavy embedding consumers). CS drafts being prepared.

Sara.k: contacting Sales/CS now — status page pinned to partial degradation for hosted API in us-west-2. Use incident template: "We're seeing elevated latency and errors for generation and embeddings in us-west-2; mitigations in progress; you may see 429s or slower responses."

Diane: I deployed a quick server-side timeout tuning: reduce per-chunk IO timeout from 20s -> 6s for streaming backends to avoid long-lived streaming holding KV cache. Command:
```
/ops/runtime/tune --pool gpu-pool-3 --streaming_io_timeout=6000
```

miguel: reroute rule applied, edge rate limits are in effect (cfg-2026-17585 applied to ~80% edges, full rollout in 30s). Early signal: p95 dropped from 6.2s -> 3.4s for non-enterprise keys; error rate down to +3% vs baseline. Queue depth trending down.

ajay: applied max_inflight=32 on gpu-pool-3. We're seeing an immediate increase in 429s from noisy tenants but overall tail latency improving in traces. Adding explicit 429 handler in gateway to return Retry-After: 10s.

incident-bot: CHANGE: runtime param update complete (max_inflight change on gpu-pool-3).

Sara.k: summary so far: edge rate limits rolled, streaming IO timeouts reduced, heavy model traffic rerouted to fallback quant variant, max_inflight lowered on affected pool. Observable effect: p95 reduced ~45%, queue depth halved. Next: decide on quota bump or sustained capacity increases for enterprise customers.

cs-lead: account-omega and account-zenith are high-touch — CS requests temporary quota bump for account-omega due to business traffic. Recommend granting targeted quota increase only if we can move them to dedicated capacity.

Diane: agreed — don't expand shared capacity. Offer temporary grace with strict token caps and place them on a monitored list.

ajay: for now I'll enable customer-scoped exemptions so enterprise keys get qps=60 while free/default stay at 8. Command:
```
POST /admin/edge/rate_limits/update
{ "rules": [{"selector":"tier:enterprise", "qps":60, "burst":200}], "change_id":"cfg-2026-17585-e1" }
```

deploy-bot: edge config update completed (cfg-2026-17585-e1).

miguel: monitoring shows enterprise tenants stable. Free-tier traffic under limits. Total errors down to +1.1% vs baseline. We're still seeing a small subgroup causing heavy KV churn — I'll add a short-lived cache prewarm to reduce misses for top-20 keys.

Sara.k: good. Next actions: 1) keep mitigations for next 2 hours and watch for regressions 2) prepare runbook entry for this overload pattern (KV cache storm + long streaming) 3) postmortem owner: miguel 4) handoff in 30m to ajay for overnight.

cs-lead: sending customer messages now. Template sent to account teams.

ajay: I'll own the handoff. If anything regresses, escalate to infra lead. Leaving a short playbook in the thread:
- If p95 climbs >3.5s -> check kv_miss_ratio and apply reroute for heavy models.
- If error rate >3% and queue depth rising -> reduce max_inflight further by 25% and tighten edge qps.
- If >5% error for enterprise keys -> roll back edge rule and increase dedicated capacity (contact infra ops).

Sara.k: handing off to ajay in 30. Recording final notes in incident tracker. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

ajay: taking over in 30. Leaving monitoring alerts at current thresholds; will sleep with pager but will escalate if >3% errors persist.

incident-bot: P1 status -> mitigated. Update posted to incident feed (incident-1758509123).
